title: Ramp Rascals - A dad and his daughter's adventure!
author: ethiopian123
selftext:
Hey everyone, hope you're all well! I'm a dad building a stunt and racing game with my daughters. It's called Ramp Rascals. Tiny RC cars, giant ramps, eight stunt arenas, eight race circuits, drifting, robot rivals, cups and a park builder. It's on Windows and Android, free, no ads, no sign-up. It's finally playable:

https://cnich1234.itch.io/ramp-rascals

THE WORKFLOW (because that's why we're here)

• I'm the director: I decide what the game is and how it should feel, play-test it, and my daughters tell me when something is wrong.

• Sonnet is the orchestrator. It keeps the bug list, plans the jobs and hands them out. It does no building itself.

• Opus writes the code (Godot / GDScript).

• Fable does the Blender 3D art, research and analysis.

• Every job is its own agent on its own git branch and worktree. Branches get merged into a release candidate, and a release agent ships it.

• There's a big automated test suite (about 2,000 tests). Agents also use a "robot driver" to measure lap times, find boost bugs and check every track, so I'm not the only tester.

WHAT WORKED

• Keeping the orchestrator out of the work, so its context stays small enough to run for days.

• Writing the bugs as short owner reports ("the boost fires twice at 0:19"), then letting an agent reproduce, fix and add a regression test.

• Measuring, not guessing: agents report numbers, like time lost per hazard hit, before and after.

WHAT WAS HARD

• Feel. The AI can tune numbers, but only a human with a controller knows when a car feels floaty. That part was me and the kids.

• Context drift on long projects. I now write handoff notes for new sessions.

• Phone quirks that only show up on a real device.

Question:

How do you all handle test suites? Initially it would run the full test suite after every small change. Well, this was fine at the beginning but it's now 1 hour at the minimum to run the full test suite. I have changed it to only run tests on code that was touched. This seems to be working much better. Full publishes get the full test suite. Anyways, curious what others do here.

I'd love your feedback on both the game and the workflow:

• Does the driving feel good?

• Which arena or circuit is your favourite, and which feels off?

• Anything broken on your phone or PC?

• How are you running agents on bigger projects?

https://cnich1234.itch.io/ramp-rascals

I will be putting on steam and Google play in the future. Itch.io will get regular updates for the time being. 

Thanks everyone and happy building!
